gotcha.title: Creating a file and expecting it to just be there
gotcha.looks_fine: In Go, the `.go` files in a package folder are compiled together (test files and files excluded by build constraints aside). Build tools for Java, Kotlin and C# typically collect a whole source folder. In those languages, create the file and it's part of the build.
gotcha.rust_sees: Rust starts at `main.rs` and only follows the `mod` lines it finds. `src/pricing.rs` exists, but nothing declared it, so it isn't part of the program.
gotcha.why: Being explicit means the module tree is written in your code, not decided by whatever files happen to be in a folder. The fix is one line, and the compiler's `help:` shows exactly which one.

fixed.name: src/main.rs
fixed.out:
3 x 1250 cents for ana
total after discounts: $33.75

go.says: In Go, the `.go` files in the package folder are included automatically (not `_test.go` files, files whose names start with `_` or `.`, or files excluded by build constraints). There's nothing to declare.

kotlin.says: In Kotlin the build gives the compiler a set of files, and files in the same package see each other without any declaration.

python.says: A Python file runs when something imports it, and not otherwise. Nothing declares it ahead of time, but nothing loads it by being in the folder either.

typescript.says: A TypeScript file is compiled when something imports it (or when `tsconfig.json` includes it). The import is the declaration.

c.says: A C file that is not listed in the build is not compiled, and the linker reports an undefined reference to what is in it. Like `mod`, the build has to be told about the file.

cpp.says: Same as C: a `.cpp` file that is not listed in the build is not compiled, and the linker complains about what is missing. Like `mod`, the build has to be told about the file.
